# SWC and Solution Planning Standards

This skill provides shared documentation standards:

- Frontend: `references/frontend-standard.md`
- Backend: `references/backend-standard.md`
- Central document (uses of SWC, IDs, test cases, manual notes, decisions): `references/swc-central.md`
- Routing and usage: `references/guide.md`
- Work log for time sheets: `references/swc-central.md` section 11

Use these standards for solution planning, SWC documentation, flowcharts and sequence diagrams across all managed systems.

## Routing

- frontend page/module/component/composable/UI flow → Frontend SWC Standard
- backend endpoint/auth/validation/data/side-effect flow → Backend API and Flow Standard
- full-stack or cross-system flow → both standards linked by the same REQ/AC and API contract

## Source Of Truth

The standards define document shape and completeness. They do not override target-project facts.

Use current source/tests/contracts for current behavior and approved REQ/AC for desired behavior. Treat framework, service and business names in examples as placeholders unless verified in the target project.

If evidence conflicts, record the conflict or Open Question. Do not invent behavior.

## Planning And Delivery

For meaningful features:

1. capture request and REQ/AC
2. discover the current system
3. complete and review the shared solution document and API contract
4. split the approved handoff into frontend and backend work
5. use the applicable standard under each side's `SWC/` folder to create its SWC
6. map implementation/tests/evidence back to the shared REQ/AC and API contract
7. keep shared documents, both SWCs and diagrams synchronized with approved implementation changes
8. write Acceptance Criteria (AC) from the REQ, then Test Cases (UT unit, IT integration) from the AC, in each page/endpoint spec
9. write Manual Notes (frontend) or Usage Notes (backend) when the feature is user-facing or called by others; mark `not needed` with a reason otherwise
10. update the Change Log, add a DEC to the module's Decision Log when direction changes, and update `traceability.md`
11. add a Work Log row for the task (see Work Log below)

Planning-only work may stop after the solution/spec/diagram stage when assumptions, open questions and unverified areas are explicit.

## Diagram Compatibility

Follow the Mermaid version rules of the destination documentation. Frontend SWC currently requires Mermaid v8.8.0 compatibility. Do not mix frontend and backend diagram syntax without verifying the target renderer.

## Central Document

`docs/SWC-CENTRAL.md` defines how SWC is reused for solution design, direction changes, user manuals, unit tests, integration tests and time sheets.

- SWC files declare `Status`, `Evidence` (Current / Proposed / POC / Verified), `REQ Refs` and `Owner` in the header when the project tracks REQ/AC (its project card says so, or REQ/AC ids already exist); otherwise only `Last Updated` (see `document-set.md`).
- Never claim `Verified` unless the check was actually run; keep mock tests separate from tests against a real database or provider.
- A manual may be written only from sections whose Evidence is Current (for a live feature) or Verified. Never publish Proposed or POC content as a manual.
- When direction changes, add a new DEC, mark affected REQs as Changed or Dropped, follow `traceability.md` to update AC, tests and manuals, and keep the old DEC as Superseded. Do not delete history.

## Work Log

At the end of every non-trivial task, append one row to `worklog/YYYY-MM-DD.md` next to the project's SWC folders (create it from `references/templates/worklog.md` if missing), then say in the final report which row was added.

- Record Start/End only from real time (for example the `date` command). If real time is unavailable, write `?` and mark `Source = Estimate`. Never invent durations.
- Agent session time is not the same as the person's working time. State that the person must review the time before it goes into a time sheet.
- `Ref` must point back to a ticket and/or REQ / AC / DEC. Do not log secrets, tokens, customer data or whole prompts.
- Rows must not overlap in time. Fix mistakes by editing the row, not by deleting the day.
